title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and follow directions, take buses and autos, and tell a driver where to go and where to stop.
intro:
Directions in Telugu are given with commands: *నేరుగా వెళ్ళండి* (go straight), *కుడి వైపు తిరగండి* (turn right). You'll learn the polite and informal **imperative** forms, and the case endings for movement: **-కి** (to), **నుంచి** (from) and **వరకు** (as far as).

In Telugu cities, the auto-rickshaw is king. Notice the typical way to hail one: *చార్మినార్ వస్తారా?* ('Will you come to Charminar?').

vocab.note: To the right: కుడి వైపు (vaipu, side).

vocab.en: up to, until, as far as

phrases.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
Auto! Will you go to Koti?
Does this bus go to Secunderabad?
I'm lost. (lit. I've lost the way)

grammar.title: Commands: polite -ండి and informal
grammar.body:
The **informal** command is the bare verb stem: *రా* (come), *చూడు* (look), *ఆగు* (wait), *వెళ్ళు* (go). Use it with close friends, children and juniors.

The **polite** (and plural) command adds **-ండి** (-ṇḍi), with -u becoming -a: *రండి*, *చూడండి*, *ఆగండి*, *వెళ్ళండి*, *తిరగండి*. This is the safe default with strangers and drivers.

**Don't!**: informal stem + **-కు** (*వెళ్ళకు*, don't go), polite stem + **-కండి** (*వెళ్ళకండి*). The word *వద్దు* can also follow a verbal noun: *వెళ్ళడం వద్దు* (no going).

grammar.title: To, from, as far as, by
grammar.body:
**Destination** takes the dative **-కి / -కు**: స్టేషనుకి (to the station), ఇంటికి (home), హైదరాబాదుకి. Here/there/where become ఇక్కడికి, అక్కడికి, ఎక్కడికి. For going to a person, use **దగ్గరికి**: *డాక్టర్ దగ్గరికి*.

**Source**: **నుంచి** (from): *ఇక్కడి నుంచి* (from here; note ఇక్కడ → ఇక్కడి). **Limit**: **వరకు** (up to): *స్టేషను వరకు*.

**Means of transport** uses **-లో** (in): *బస్సులో*, *రైల్లో*, *ఆటోలో*. On foot is *నడిచి* ('having walked').

examples.native: స్టేషను నుంచి ఇంటి వరకు ఆటోలో వచ్చాను.
examples.roman: sṭēṣanu nunchi iṇṭi varaku āṭōlō vachchānu.
examples.en: I came from the station to the house by auto.
Tomorrow I'll go to Vijayawada by train.
How far is it from here?

dialogue.title: To Charminar
dialogue.setting: A visitor asks a passer-by the way to Charminar in Hyderabad, then takes an auto.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.en: Excuse me, how do I get to Charminar?

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.native: ఇక్కడి నుంచి కొంచెం దూరం. ఆటోలో వెళ్ళండి.
lines.roman: ikkaḍi nunchi konchem dūram. āṭōlō veḷḷaṇḍi.
lines.en: It's a bit far from here. Take an auto.

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.native: వెళ్ళొచ్చు, కానీ అరగంట పడుతుంది. ఈ రోడ్డులో నేరుగా వెళ్ళి, సిగ్నల్ దగ్గర ఎడమ వైపు తిరగండి.
lines.roman: veḷḷochchu, kānī aragaṇṭa paḍutundi. ī rōḍḍulō nērugā veḷḷi, signal daggara eḍama vaipu tiragaṇḍi.
lines.en: You can, but it takes half an hour. Go straight down this road and turn left at the signal.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.en: Thank you. Auto! Will you go to Charminar?

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.en: That much? Put the meter on.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.en: Stop here, please. How much is it?

culture: Directions in Telugu towns are given by **landmarks** rather than street names: 'past the temple, opposite the bank, next to the big tamarind tree'. Many neighbourhood names end in *-పేట* (pēṭa, town), *-పల్లి* (palli, village), *-గూడ* (gūḍa) or *-నగర్* (nagar). Auto drivers often quote a fixed fare; asking for the meter, or using a ride-hailing app, is normal.
